newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Bank of Scotland boosts market share.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bank of Scotland boosts market share.

text.p: Bank of Scotland said on Wednesday its first half pre-tax profits rose a bumper 24 percent to 324.3 million pounds ($508 million), beating analysts' forecasts of between 283 and 305 million pounds.
It raised its dividend by 18.8 percent to 2.91 pence per share from 2.45, saying it continued to gain market share in Britain and the picture in most of its markets remained bright.
Analysts said they were likely to upgrade their full-year profit forecasts to around 650 to 660 million pounds after seeing the first-half performance.

"They beat expectations on income and on the costs side but that was slightly offset by some disappointment by the performance of BankWest," HSBC James Capel banking analyst David Raye said. BankWest is the group's Australian operation.

Raye said Bank of Scotland shares were cheap in the short term but longer-term considerations should be considered. These include the question of whether the bank can keep its bad debt charges so low and maintain current margins.
The bank's governor, Bruce Pattullo, said it was seeing growth across its business and strongly defended the recent high level of cost growth, saying it was already paying back.
"There's nothing wrong with spending money if you are getting a pay-back," Pattullo told Reuters in an interview. "We think we can afford to invest money. In fact, it would be criminal not to."

Taking out the effects of last year's one-off 23.6 million pound gain from the sale of a 50 percent stake in Halifax Credit Card and this year's inclusion of its recent Australian acquisition, BankWest, the underlying rise was also 24 percent.
Pattullo said Bank of Scotland had no plans for further major acquisitions, describing BankWest as a "once and for all".
"These results were achieved against generally benign economic conditions in the UK and USA with slightly more difficult conditions in Australia and New Zealand," the bank said in a statement.
Pattullo said the recent rise in costs at the bank had been an historic "quantum leap" which would not always be repeated, whereas it had produced a very early and continuing pay-back.

"If you strip out the costs associated with BankWest, costs have gone up 15 percent," Pattullo said. "But net interest income is up 16 percent and non-interest income is up 19 percent. It's that juxtapositioon that's the important thing."
Bank of Scotland's cost-to-income ratio rose to 52.9 percent, compared with 52.1 percent at the end of the last financial year, and would have been 51.3 percent excluding BankWest.

Its tier one capital ratio rose to 6.3 percent from 6.1 percent in February and Pattullo said this was in "remarkably good order". He pointed to the bank's ability to generate capital, adding this was also reflected in its dividend increase.

The integration of BankWest was proceeding as planned, he said, adding that the bank was suffering from a price battle in the Australian residential mortgage market but was performing better than expected in other areas.
In its British markets, Pattullo said conditions remain competitive in an environment characterised by a surplus of capital coupled with only moderate economic activity.
But he noted that margins in the mortgage market had stabilised and had actually widened in the first half compared with the second six months of the previous year. ($1=.6385 Pound)
